# The Fizz language: reference

The formal reference, from the language's design doc. Read `language.md` first: it teaches the text form. Come here for an exact rule or an error code. JSON field names and the text form's `name=value` attributes are the same words.

## Schema

```ts
type Score = {
  bpm: number;              // 40–240
  key: string;              // tonic only: "C", "F#", "Bb"
  scale: "major" | "minor" | "dorian" | "phrygian" | "lydian" | "mixolydian";
  swing?: number;           // 0–0.5: off-beat 16ths land this fraction of a 16th late (1/3 ≈ triplet)
  sections: Section[];      // played in order
};
type Section = {
  label: string;
  bars: number;             // 1–64
  chords: string[];         // one per bar, cycled to fill the section; "i:2" holds two bars
  layers: Layer[];
};
type Layer = {
  role: "kick" | "snare" | "hat" | "clap" | "rim" | "bass" | "chords" | "lead" | "pad" | "fx";
  instrument: string;       // a catalogue id
  steps?: 8 | 12 | 16 | 24 | 32;   // per bar, default 16
  octave?: number;          // octave of degree 1, 0–7; default by role: bass 2, chords 3, pad 3, lead 4, fx 4
  pattern: string;          // step string, below
  chance?: number;          // 0–1, each hit plays with this probability (Strudel degradeBy)
  width?: number;           // 0–1 stereo width (Strudel jux)
  lfo?: { param: string; min: number; max: number; bars: number };  // one slow sweep of one fx
  fx?: { gain?, lpf?, hpf?, lpq?, room?, size?, delay?, pan?, crush?, shape?, attack?, release? };
};
```

The zod schema (`ScoreSchema`) is structural only; every musical check is the
validator's, so the model gets a message it can act on instead of a zod error.

### Chords

Roman numerals in the key: uppercase major, lowercase minor, `°` (or `o`,
`dim`) diminished, `+` augmented; suffix `7`, `maj7`, `sus2`, `sus4`. A numeral
must have the quality the key gives that degree (`ii` in C major, not `II`),
with two exceptions: in a minor-family key (minor, dorian, phrygian) `V`, `V7`
and `vii°` use the raised 7th, and a `b`/`#` prefix marks a borrowed chord
(`bVII`), which is a warning. Chord names (`Am`, `Fmaj7`, `G7`, `Bdim`,
`Csus4`, `Bm7b5`) are accepted too; a name with notes outside the key is a
warning. `i:2` holds a chord for two bars. The list cycles to fill the section.

### Pitch

Pitched layers write scale degrees: `1`–`7`, `'` per octave up, `,` per octave
down, `b`/`#` for an accidental (a warning, except `#7` in a section that has a
dominant chord in a minor-family key). `x` on a pitched layer plays the bar's
chord: all of it for `chords`/`pad`, its root for `bass`/`lead`/`fx`. A bass of
`x` steps follows the progression with no pitch written at all.

### Rhythm: the step string

```
pattern := bar ("|" bar)*        bars cycle to fill the section
step    := x | X | . | _ | degree | [a b] | <a b ...>
```

| Step | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x` / `X` | hit / accented hit |
| `.` | rest |
| `_` | hold the previous note one more step (ties over a bar line); on an unpitched layer it sustains the hit (noise beds, open hats) |
| `[ab]` | one step split in two (32nd pairs, ghost notes): `[xx]`, `[x.]`, `[1 3]` |
| `<a b>` | `a` the first time the bar plays, `b` the second, … |

Whitespace is free (`x... x...` = `x...x...`). Every bar must have exactly
`steps` steps; a split counts as one.

## Text form

A readable view of the same score, lossless both ways
(`parseText(printText(s))` deep-equals `s`; property-tested over 500 random
scores including awkward strings). JSON is what the model writes and what is
stored; the text form is for people, diffs and docs.

```
fizz score v0
bpm 124
key A minor
swing 0.2                     (only when set)

section "drop" bars=16
  chords: i:4 VI:2 VII:2
    kick 909_bd gain=0.95 : x... x... x... x...
    hat 909_hh chance=0.9 gain=0.3 hpf=400 : xxXx xxXx xxXx xxXx
    pad gm_pad_warm octave=3 lfo=lpf,600,2400,8 room=0.6 : x___ ____ ____ ____
```

A layer line is `role[#id] instrument [attr=value…] : pattern`. Attributes are
`steps`, `octave`, `chance`, `width`, `enter`, `exit`, `humanize`, `glide`,
`lfo=param,min,max,bars`, `ramp=param,from,to` (repeatable; `ramp=[]` for an
empty list), `presence`/`tone`/`space`/`voicing=word`, and each fx as
`name=value` (`fx={}` for an empty fx object). A section line may add
`key=` and `scale=`; the header may add `seed N`. Comments start with `# `. Strings that wouldn't survive as
a bare word are written as JSON strings.

## Fizz v1

`compile(source)` = `expand()` → `normalise()` → `validate(…, { v1: true })`.
The composer path (`convex/fizzComposer.ts`) runs it on every model answer.
Text with the header `fizz score v1` is v1 source (`parseSource`), and
`parseText` expands it; text headed `fizz score v0` is flat and reads verbatim.

**Bounds.** No loops, conditionals or recursion. A phrase can't use a phrase,
a `from` chain can't loop and is at most 8 sections deep. Expansion caps:
64 `form` entries, 1,024 bars, 4,096 characters per expanded pattern, 32
phrases of at most 512 characters. Errors name the flat path and, where expansion moved it, the source
path: `sections[2].layers[0].pattern (written at sections[0].layers[0].pattern): …`.

### Reliability rules

| Rule | Text | JSON |
|---|---|---|
| **One step, one glued character.** In a run with no spaces each character is a step. A step written with more than one character (`[xx]`, `<x .>`, `5,`, `1'`, `b3`, `5!`, `~5`, `$hook`) stands alone with spaces round it. A bar that miscounts with such a step glued in gets `E_GLUED`, whose message gives the spaced fix; a glued bar that counts right is accepted (the rule exists to stop miscounts). v1 only, and on an edit only for patterns the edit wrote. | `x.x. [xx] ...` · `1 . 5, .` | same strings |
| `r` is a one-character roll, the same as `[xx]`. | `..x. .xr.` | `"..x. .xr."` |
| Bars on their own lines, numbers optional and checked (`2|` on the third bar is a parse error). | `lead kalimba :` then `  1| 1 . 3 .…` `  2| …` | `"pattern": ["1 . 3 .…", "…"]` |

**Normalisation before repair** (each with a `W_NORMALISED` or `W_UNUSED` warning;
most came from what the v1 composer runs got wrong first time):
`_` after a rest becomes a rest; a bar one or two steps short that ends in a
rest or hold is padded with that step, and one or two steps long with only
rests in the surplus is trimmed (earlier steps keep their places; other
miscounts stay errors); when `steps` is left out and every bar is
8 or 32 steps, `steps` is set (a written `steps` is kept); room, delay and
width on kick or bass are dropped (new tracks only); an inherited layer
entering past a shorter section's end leaves it, and an exit past the end is
the end; a ramp from a value to the same value is removed; a section with no
`from` and `chords: []` carries on the previous section's progression; in
`attrs` a repeated key keeps its last value and `name=none` is skipped;
dropping a layer that isn't there, or `drop` without `from`, is a warning. On
an edit, `"sections": []` keeps the stored sections and `swing: 0` on a score
without swing is dropped. `compile` never shows `W_PENDING_PACK`.
`strict` (score field, or `compile(…, { strict: true })`) makes the remaining
warnings errors.

**Locating messages** (the three llm.md §4 rewrites):

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `E_STEP_COUNT` | `bar 1 has 15 of 16 steps. Groups: "...." 4, "...." 4, "X..." 4, ".x[xx]" 3 — a [..] pair is ONE step. Make ".x[xx]" 4 steps` |
| `E_STEP_COUNT` (every bar) | `every bar has 8 steps but the layer is 16. If you meant eighth notes, set "steps": 8 and keep the pattern; otherwise make each bar 16 steps` |
| `E_HOLD` | `the bar, step 4: "_" after "." holds nothing ("X_._"). To rest write "X_..", to re-hit write "X_.X", to keep ringing write "X___"` |
| `E_GLUED` | `the bar has 15 of 16 steps, and "[xx]" is glued into ".x[xx]". One glued character is one step; … Write ".xr" (r is a roll) or ".x [xx]", then count again` |
| `E_SHAPE` | the path is printed once (`- bpm: Invalid input: …`), not twice |

### Structure

| Construct | Text | JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Layer id, unique in its section; default is the role, numbered on repeats (`hat`, `hat2`) | `hat#open 909_oh : ..x. ..x. ..x. ..x.` | `{ "id": "open", "role": "hat", … }` |
| Form: play order, labels may repeat | `form: intro verse chorus verse chorus` | `"form": ["intro", "verse", "chorus", "verse", "chorus"]` |
| Section reuse: the base's bars, chords and layers; fields given replace the base's; `chords: []` keeps the base's; a `from` section can be a base | `section chorus from=verse` | `{ "label": "chorus", "from": "verse" }` |
| Per-id override: only the fields written change (`fx` is replaced whole) | `  #hook gain=0.5 : $hook+3` | `{ "id": "hook", "fx": {"gain": 0.5}, "pattern": "$hook+3" }` |
| Leave base layers out | `section break from=drop drop=kick,hat` | `"drop": ["kick", "hat"]` |
| Named phrase, used as `$name`, moved by scale steps with `$name+n` / `$name-n` (octaves carry) | `phrase hook = 1 . 3 5 1' _ 5 _` · `lead : $hook $hook+3` | `"phrases": [{ "name": "hook", "pattern": "1 . 3 5 1' _ 5 _" }]` |
| Enter / exit: first and last bar (from 1) the layer plays in its section | `lead kalimba enter=5 exit=8 : …` | `"enter": 5, "exit": 8` |

`form` copies each section into the flat `sections` list, so the stored score
is flat. A section left out of `form` (and not used by a `from`) is `W_UNUSED`,
as is a phrase never used.

### Expression

| Construct | Text | JSON | Flat result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ghost hit / accent | `g` / `X` | same | `ScoreEvent.velocity` 0.35 / 1 (plain 0.75) |
| Accent / ghost on a degree | `5!` / `5?` | same | velocity 1 / 0.35 |
| Glide into a note | `~5`, `glide=0.08` | `"~5"`, `"glide": 0.08` | `ScoreEvent.glide` seconds (default 0.1) |
| One-way automation, several params | `ramp=hpf,200,6000 ramp=gain,0.2,0.9` | `"ramp": [{ "param": "hpf", "from": 200, "to": 6000 }, …]` | layer `ramp` (linear over the layer's bars in the section) |
| Humanize, seeded | `humanize=0.3`, `seed 7` | `"humanize": 0.3`, `"seed": 7` | layer `humanize`, score `seed` |
| Voicing | `voicing=led\|open\|spread\|close` | `"voicing": "open"` | resolved into `ScoreEvent.midi` |
| Slash chord: that chord tone in the bass | `chords: I V/3 vi IV` | `["I", "V/3", "vi", "IV"]` | chords/pad stack it lowest; a bass `x` plays it |
| Key change per section | `section lift from=chorus key=B` | `{ "key": "B", "scale": "major" }` | section `key`/`scale`; `analyse` resolves pitches in it |
| Tone / presence defaults (score or section) | `tone dark` · `section verse tone=warm` | `"tone": "dark"` | pushed onto every layer that has none; tone skips drums |

Chords and pads are voice-led (`led`: the inversion nearest the previous
chord, within a fifth of root position) when `compile` runs with
`defaults: true`, as it does for a new track. Edits run without defaults, and
a flat score with no `voicing` keeps v0's root position, so stored tracks and
the seeds sound as they did.

## v1 engine contract

Fizz v1 (`docs/roadmap/fizz-v1-the-language.md`) is shorthand that expands to the
flat JSON above, plus these plain optional fields. A v0 score sets none of them and
plays exactly as before. The engine card (`fizz-v1-the-engine-plays-it`) builds on them.

| Where | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| score | `seed?: number` | whole number seeding `humanize` and `chance`; the track plays the same every time |
| section | `key?`, `scale?` | the section's own key; `analyse` resolves every pitch in it (`SectionAnalysis.key`/`.scale`) |
| layer | `id?: string` | a name unique in its section (`hat#open`); defaults to the role |
| layer | `enter?`, `exit?: number` | first and last bar (from 1) the layer plays in its section; `analyse` emits no events outside |
| layer | `ramp?: { param, from, to }[]` | one-way linear automation of an fx param (gain lpf hpf lpq room delay pan crush shape) from the start of the layer's first bar to the end of its last bar in the section; coexists with `lfo` on a different param |
| layer | `humanize?: number` | 0–1: seeded timing (up to ±10 ms at 1) and velocity jitter (up to ±0.15 at 1) |
| layer | `voicing?: "close" \| "led" \| "open" \| "spread"` | how `x` on chords/pad stacks the chord; resolved into `ScoreEvent.midi` by `analyse`. Absent = close (v0); the v1 composer path sets `led` |
| layer | `glide?: number` | seconds a `~` note slides from the previous note (default 0.1) |
| event | `ScoreEvent.velocity: number` | the written dynamic: ghost (`g`, `5?`) 0.35, plain 0.75, accent (`X`, `5!`) 1 |
| event | `ScoreEvent.glide?: number` | seconds of portamento into this note; absent when it doesn't glide |

## Error catalogue

`validate()` returns `{ errors, warnings }`; each issue is `{ path, code, message }`. Errors (`E_`) make the score invalid; warnings (`W_`) are reported and the score still plays. The messages below are real validator output, so the wording is what the composer sees in a repair round.

| Code | Example input | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `E_SHAPE` | `bpm` | bpm: Invalid input: expected number, received string |
| `E_BPM` | `bpm` | bpm is 300; tempo runs 40–240 |
| `E_KEY` | `key` | key "A minor" is not a note; write the tonic only, like C, F#, Bb (the mode goes in "scale") |
| `E_SWING` | `swing` | swing is 0.8; swing runs 0–0.5 (1/3 ≈ triplet feel) |
| `E_NO_SECTIONS` | `sections` | a score needs at least one section |
| `E_SECTION_BARS` | `sections[0].bars` | section "verse" has bars 0; bars is a whole number 1–64 |
| `E_NO_CHORDS` | `sections[0].chords` | section "verse" has no chords; give at least one, e.g. ["i:2", "VI:2"] |
| `E_BAD_CHORD` | `sections[0].chords[1]` | "Xyz" is not a chord. Write a roman numeral in the key (i, iv, V7, bVII, vii°) or a chord name (Am, Fmaj7, G7, Bdim, Csus4) |
| `E_CHORD_NOT_IN_KEY` | `sections[0].chords[1]` | "II" is not in A minor: the chord on degree 2 is diminished here, write "ii°". For a chord borrowed from the parallel key (minor iv in a major key), write its name instead, e.g. "B" |
| `E_CHORD_HOLD` | `sections[0].chords[0]` | "i:0": the hold after ":" is a whole number of bars ≥ 1 |
| `E_UNKNOWN_INSTRUMENT` | `sections[0].layers[0].instrument` | unknown instrument "rhodes"; use a catalogue id exactly. For role chords, closest: gm_epiano1, sine, square, sawtooth, triangle |
| `E_ROLE_INSTRUMENT` | `sections[0].layers[0].role` | "909_bd" can't play role snare; it plays kick or fx. For snare try: 909_sd, 808_sd, dmx_sd, sd, mpc60_sd |
| `E_STEPS` | `sections[0].layers[0].steps` | steps is 10; a bar has 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32 steps |
| `E_OCTAVE` | `sections[0].layers[0].octave` | octave is 9; it is a whole number 0–7 |
| `E_PATTERN` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | pattern: "[xxx]" splits a step into 3; a split holds exactly two, like [xx] or [1 3] |
| `E_STEP_COUNT` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | the bar has 17 of 16 steps. Groups: "x..." 4, "x..." 4, "x..." 4, "x..." 4, "x" 1. Add or remove steps so it has exactly 16 |
| `E_DEGREE` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | degree 8 is out of the scale; degrees run 1–7, write 1' for the octave above and 7, for the 7th below |
| `E_PITCH_ON_DRUM` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | "1" is a pitch but 909_bd is unpitched; drum layers use x, X and . |
| `E_HOLD` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | the bar, step 4: "_" after "." holds nothing ("X_._"). To rest write "X_..", to re-hit write "X_.X", to keep ringing write "X___" |
| `E_FX_UNKNOWN` | `sections[0].layers[0].fx.reverb` | unknown fx "reverb"; fx are gain, lpf, hpf, lpq, room, size, delay, pan, crush, shape, attack, release |
| `E_FX_RANGE` | `sections[0].layers[0].fx.lpf` | fx.lpf is 50000; lpf runs 20–20000 (low-pass cutoff in Hz; lower = darker) |
| `E_RANGE` | `sections[0].layers[0].chance` | chance is 2; it runs 0–1 |
| `E_LFO` | `sections[0].layers[0].lfo` | lfo on lpf sweeps 500–500; it needs two different values inside 20–20000 (min > max sweeps down) |
| `E_LAYER_ID` | `sections[0].layers[1].id` | two layers in section "a" are called "a" (layers 0 and 1); ids are unique in a section, rename one |
| `E_ENTER_EXIT` | `sections[0].layers[0].enter` | enter is 5; it is a bar of the section, a whole number 1–4 |
| `E_RAMP` | `sections[0].layers[0].ramp[0].param` | ramp.param "size" can't be automated; use one of gain, lpf, hpf, lpq, room, delay, pan, crush, shape |
| `E_GLUED` (v1) | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | the bar has 15 of 16 steps, and "[xx]" is glued into ".x[xx]". One glued character is one step; a bracket group or marked degree stands alone with spaces around it. Write ".xr" (r is a roll) or ".x [xx]", then count again |
| `E_FORM` (v1) | `form[1]` | form plays "x", which isn't a section; labels are "a" |
| `E_FROM` (v1) | `sections[1].from` | section "b" is from "c", which leads back to "b"; a from chain can't loop |
| `E_PHRASE` (v1) | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | "$nope" is not a phrase; define it in phrases first |
| `E_EXPANDED_SIZE` (v1) | `form` | the score expands to 1088 bars; at most 1024 |
| `W_ACCIDENTAL` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | "b2" is outside A minor; fine for a passing or leading note, otherwise use the plain degree |
| `W_BORROWED_CHORD` | `sections[0].chords[1]` | "bII" is borrowed from outside A minor; fine if intended (also: "iv" in C major is borrowed from the parallel key of C major; fine if intended) |
| `W_CHORD_OUT_OF_KEY` | `sections[0].chords[1]` | "D7" has 1 note(s) outside A minor; fine if intended, or pick a chord from the key |
| `W_PENDING_PACK` | `sections[0].layers[0].instrument` | "linndrum_bd" needs the drum sample pack (pending); it will fall back to a synthesized kit |
| `W_PATTERN_BARS` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | the pattern has 3 bars but the section is 4; it restarts mid-way |
| `W_CHORD_BARS` | `sections[0].chords` | the chords cover 3 bars but the section is 4; the progression restarts mid-way |
| `W_SILENT_LAYER` | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | the kick layer never plays; remove it or add hits |
| `W_NORMALISED` (v1) | `sections[0].layers[0].pattern` | "_" after a rest held nothing; it now rests |
| `W_UNUSED` (v1) | `phrases` | phrase "a" is never used; use it as $a or remove it |

### Musical findings (lint)

`lint(score)` (`packages/score/src/lint.ts`, or `compile(…, { lint: true })` as `findings`) returns the musical checks in the same issue shape, all warnings: the score still plays, and a deliberate blue note is allowed. They are kept apart from the validator's warnings (and from `strict`). `fizz check` prints them with the line (a bar line where the pattern is written one bar per line) and `--strict` fails on them; the composer sends `W_OFF_CHORD_STRONG` back once (its other findings go into the result's `warnings`); `scripts/fizz-tracks-lint.test.ts` fails CI on any `W_OFF_CHORD_STRONG` in a shipped track. One finding of a kind per layer.

| Code | Path | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `W_OFF_CHORD_STRONG` | `sections[0].layers[4].pattern[0]` | lead, bar 4 beat 1: Ab over Cm7. Land on chord tones on beats 1 and 3: move it to C, Eb, G or Bb, or put a hook that must fit every chord on a chords layer |
| `W_REPEATED_RHYTHM` | `sections[0].layers[4]` | lead plays the same rhythm two bars running. Vary it: write 2 or 4 different bars in the pattern |
| `W_REVERB_ON_BASS` | `sections[0].layers[1]` | room or delay on the bass muddies the low end. Take them off the bass |
| `W_ONE_OCTAVE` | `sections` | every note sits inside one octave. Spread the registers: bass at octave 1–2, chords at 3, lead at 4–5 |
| `W_LEAD_NO_MOTIF` | `sections[0].layers[2]` | the lead never repeats a 3-note shape. State a motif, repeat it with one change, answer it, return |
| `W_SINGLE_CHORD_VAMP` (song-form brief only) | `sections[0].chords` | fewer than 3 distinct chords in a song-form track. Write a real progression: 3 or more chords, ending on V → i or V → I |

`W_OFF_CHORD_STRONG` checks `bass`, `chords`, `lead` and `pad` (not `fx` or drums): the note sounding on step 1 or 9 (the half bar for other step counts), a held or glided note counting as the note it continues, against the bar's chord tones (the triad, the 7th when the symbol has one, a slash chord's bass).
